FAQ

Frequently asked questions.

Which ad platforms does Maradar connect to?

Maradar connects to Meta and Google ad accounts via official OAuth integrations. Additional platforms are on the roadmap, reach out to ask about your specific setup.

How quickly will I see useful insights after connecting?

Your first insights are ready about 30 minutes after connecting. The more data available, the more specific the recommendations, and intelligence improves the longer you use it.

What's different about Maradar versus just using my platform dashboards?

Platform dashboards show you what happened. Maradar tells you why — whether it was creative fatigue or competitive pressure. It also surfaces insights from competitor ads and market intelligence that platform dashboards don't have access to.

Can I monitor multiple markets and competitor brands?

Yes. Markets and competitor brands monitored scale with your plan (35 competitor brands on Starter, up to 150 on Scale tier).

Is my performance data shared with other brands?

Never. Your performance data is yours alone and is never shared with, compared to, or used to improve recommendations for other brands. Where we identify patterns across the platform, we use only anonymised, aggregated data — individual brand data is fully isolated.

What are AI actions used for?

AI actions power Ask Maradar queries, brief generation, and deep analysis reports. Each intelligence query costs 1 action.

Can I change my plan or cancel anytime?

Yes — upgrade or downgrade anytime. No long-term contract. Cancel with no penalties. Terms apply.

OUR STORY

We built the tool we wished we had.

Building Maradar. Somewhere between the 40th brand audit and the 400th post-mortem.

Between us, we've spent decades running marketing across APAC, from 4As agencies to brands to Meta. We managed ads strategy, insights, and solutions for hundreds of brands across the region.

Every single time, the same problem showed up. The data was there. The answer wasn't. Brands were spending hours in post-mortems that led nowhere. Smart marketers making gut-feel calls dressed up as strategy. Not because they were bad at marketing — because no tool connected the dots across the data sources that actually mattered.

We didn't build Maradar to replace marketers, we help them to be more strategic. We built it so the answer is already there when you walk in the room.

The moment we decided to actually build it. Somewhere between the second and third round.

Louise Leong
Co-Founder, Strategy & Growth
4As Agencies→ Sales & Marketing→ Meta Global & APAC→ Maradar

"The best marketing and advertising decision is the one you make with confidence. We built Maradar so you always have a reason."

Sean Chui
Co-Founder, Product & Technology
Agency→ Martech→ Meta→ Maradar

"Every marketer deserves the same intelligence that Fortune 500s pay consultants for. That's the whole point."

Privacy Policy

Last updated May 5, 2026

This Privacy Policy describes how Maradar Limited ("we," "us," or "our") accesses, collects, stores, uses, or shares ("processes") your personal information when you visit our website, register for the Services, connect third-party platforms to your account, communicate with us, or otherwise interact with our Services.

Questions or concerns? Reading this Privacy Policy will help you understand your privacy rights and choices. We are responsible for making decisions about how your personal information is processed. If you do not agree with our policies and practices, please do not use our Services.

Summary of Key Points

What personal information do we process? We process the business contact information and account credentials you provide during registration, as well as the advertising performance data and creative assets from third-party platforms (such as Meta and Google) that you explicitly authorize via OAuth. We do not collect personal data of your end customers or consumers, and we do not collect special categories of sensitive personal data.

Do we process any sensitive personal information? We do not process sensitive personal information.

How do we process your information? We process your information to provide, improve, and administer our Services, communicate with you, for security and fraud prevention, and to comply with law.

In what situations and with which parties do we share personal information? We may share information in specific situations and with specific third parties. We do not sell your data or share it with third parties for their independent commercial use.

What are your rights? Depending on where you are located geographically, the applicable privacy law may mean you have certain rights regarding your personal information. Contact us at admin@maradar.ai to exercise them.

1. What Information Do We Collect?

We collect information necessary to provide our B2B ads and creative intelligence services. We focus on business-related data and do not seek to collect information about your personal life outside of your professional use of the platform.

  • (a) Account Information. When you register, we collect your name, email address, and a securely hashed password. We do not store your password in plain text.
  • (b) Connected Platform Data. When you authorize Maradar to connect to a third-party advertising platform via OAuth, we receive authentication tokens, advertising creative content, advertising performance metrics, and campaign configuration metadata. We do not ingest underlying audience lists or customer email lists from connected platforms.
  • (c) Brand and Business Information. Information you provide about your business and brand through onboarding flows or direct communications.
  • (d) Service Interaction Data. Feedback on Service outputs, queries you submit, and operational logs necessary to deliver, maintain, and improve the Services.
  • (e) Usage and Technical Information. IP address, browser type, device information, and usage patterns within the platform.
  • (f) Communications. Information you provide when contacting us, including support requests and feedback.
  • (g) Payment Information. We do not collect or store payment card information. Payment processing is handled by Airwallex Limited under their independent privacy practices.
  • (h) Future Categories. As the Services evolve, additional categories may be processed. We will update this Privacy Policy before any new category of processing begins.

Sensitive Information. The Services are not designed to process special categories of personal data. If your use case involves regulated personal data, contact us at admin@maradar.ai before using the Services for such purposes.

1A. What We Do Not Collect

  • We do not ingest underlying audience lists or customer email lists from connected advertising platforms — only campaign configuration and aggregated performance.
  • We do not collect, store, or process payment card data.
  • We do not request or store biometric data or precise geolocation.
  • We do not directly process information from sources or platforms beyond those described in Section 1, although we may add new sources in the future with prior disclosure.

2. How Do We Process Your Information?

In Short: We process your information to deliver the Services, improve and develop the platform, ensure security, and comply with applicable law.

  • To deliver the Services to you. Data from connected platforms is processed to provide you with the features, analysis, and capabilities within your Maradar account. This data is specific to your account and is never made accessible to other customers in identifiable form.
  • To operate, improve, and develop the platform. We may use data generated through your use of the Services — on an aggregated and anonymised basis — to maintain and improve the Maradar platform and develop new capabilities. This use does not identify you or your brand. Data sourced from connected third-party platforms is not transferred to external parties for independent use.
  • To communicate with you. We use your contact information to send service notifications, account alerts, and product updates.
  • For security and fraud prevention. We process information as necessary to protect the security and integrity of the platform and to prevent misuse.
  • To comply with applicable law. We process information where required by law or regulation.
  • To protect your data. We implement appropriate security measures including encryption of data in transit and at rest, access controls, and security monitoring.

For full details on aggregated and anonymised data and sub-processors, see the Data Processing Addendum in our Terms of Service.

3. When and With Whom Do We Share Your Personal Information?

In Short: We may share information in specific situations with the following parties. We do not sell your data or share it with third parties for their independent commercial use.

  • Authorized Sub-processors. We share data with a limited number of service providers (cloud hosting, AI processing, payment processing) who are contractually bound to protect your data and prohibited from using it for any other purpose. A full list is available in Section 25 of our Terms of Service.
  • Legal Compliance. We may disclose information where legally required to comply with applicable law, regulatory or governmental requests, or valid legal process.
  • Business Transfers. We may share or transfer information in connection with any merger, sale of company assets, or acquisition of all or a portion of our business.

4. Do We Use Cookies and Other Tracking Technologies?

In Short: We may use cookies and other tracking technologies to collect and store your information.

We may use cookies and similar tracking technologies (like web beacons and pixels) to gather information when you interact with our Services. We maintain a strict separation between our marketing website and our authenticated platform.

On our marketing website (maradar.ai), we may also permit advertising and remarketing technologies (such as Meta and Google pixels) to identify users we have previously engaged with so that Maradar can deliver relevant advertisements about Maradar's services on third-party platforms. We do not allow third-party advertising networks to set cookies within our authenticated application (app.maradar.ai), and we do not sell or share personal information for cross-context behavioural advertising.

For full details, see our Cookie Policy (Cookie tab above). You can manage your preferences or opt out of non-essential cookies at any time through our cookie consent banner or your browser settings.

5. How Do We Handle Your Social Logins?

Maradar does not currently offer social media login. Users register and authenticate using email address and password only.

6. Is Your Information Transferred Internationally?

In Short: Your information may be transferred to, stored by, and processed in countries where Maradar's infrastructure and sub-processors operate.

Maradar's primary database operates from AWS Asia Pacific Singapore region (ap-southeast-1) via Supabase, with related Service operations performed by sub-processors located in the United States and other regions, as listed in our Terms of Service Section 25.

We have designed our Services with reference to the EU/UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) as a leading global framework, and we provide data subject rights consistent with GDPR principles globally where practicable. We also seek to comply with applicable data protection regimes including the Hong Kong Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (PDPO), the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), the Singapore Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), and the Indonesian Law on Personal Data Protection (UU PDP No. 27/2022).

For cross-border transfers, our sub-processor agreements incorporate Standard Contractual Clauses (including the UK International Data Transfer Addendum where applicable). Contact admin@maradar.ai for further information or specific sub-processor DPA copies.

7. How Long Do We Keep Your Information?

During your active subscription, we retain Customer Data for as long as necessary to provide the Services.

After your subscription terminates or is cancelled, we retain Customer Data for a default period of 30 days to allow data export and account restoration. Following this 30-day period, we delete identifiable Customer Data from our active systems within a further 60 days. Routine system backups are deleted in the ordinary course of our backup rotation, typically within 90 days from the original deletion request.

Aggregated and anonymised data may be retained indefinitely as part of our service operation. We may retain certain account information beyond these periods where required by law, to enforce our legal rights, prevent fraud, or assist with investigations.

8. Do We Collect Information From Minors?

In Short: We do not knowingly collect data from or market to children under 18 years of age.

We do not knowingly collect, solicit data from, or market to children under 18 years of age, nor do we knowingly sell such personal information. By using the Services, you represent that you are at least 18 and possess the legal authority to use the Services on behalf of your business entity. If we learn that personal information from users less than 18 years of age has been collected, we will deactivate the account and take reasonable measures to promptly delete such data. If you become aware of any data we may have collected from children under age 18, please contact us at admin@maradar.ai.

9. What Are Your Privacy Rights?

In Short: You may review, change, or terminate your account at any time, depending on your country, province, or state of residence.

Withdrawing your consent: If we are relying on your consent to process your personal information, you have the right to withdraw your consent at any time by contacting us using the details provided in Section 12 below. Please note this will not affect the lawfulness of processing before its withdrawal.

Account Information

If you would at any time like to review or change the information in your account or terminate your account, you can contact us at admin@maradar.ai or log in to your account settings. Upon your request to terminate your account, we will deactivate or delete your account and information from our active databases, subject to our retention obligations.

Jurisdiction-Specific Rights

Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have additional rights under applicable law. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at admin@maradar.ai. Verified requests will be processed within 30 days, unless a shorter timeframe is mandated by applicable law.

  • EEA, UK, or Switzerland: Under GDPR and Swiss Data Protection Laws, you may have rights to access, rectify, erase, restrict processing of, or port your personal data; object to processing; withdraw consent; and lodge a complaint with your local supervisory authority.
  • California residents: Under the CCPA, you may have rights to know, delete, correct, and opt out of "sale" or "share" of personal information. Maradar does not sell or share personal information for cross-context behavioural advertising.
  • Asia-Pacific region (HK PDPO, Singapore PDPA, Indonesia UU PDP, Malaysia PDPA): You have rights to access, correction, and withdrawal of consent. Contact us at admin@maradar.ai to exercise these rights.

10. Controls for Do-Not-Track Features

Most web browsers and some mobile operating systems include a Do-Not-Track ("DNT") feature you can activate to signal your privacy preference not to have data about your online browsing activities monitored and collected. At this stage, no uniform technology standard for recognising and implementing DNT signals has been finalised. As such, we do not currently respond to DNT browser signals. If a standard for online tracking is adopted that we must follow in the future, we will inform you about that practice in a revised version of this Privacy Policy.

11. Do We Make Updates to This Notice?

In Short: Yes, we will update this notice as necessary to stay compliant with relevant laws.

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. The updated version will be indicated by an updated date at the top of this Privacy Policy. If we make material changes, we may notify you by prominently posting a notice or by directly sending you a notification. We encourage you to review this Privacy Policy frequently.

12. How Can You Contact Us About This Notice?

If you have questions or comments about this notice, you may contact us at:

Maradar Limited, Room 303, The Ozone, 134 Wai Yip Street, Kwun Tong, Kowloon, Hong Kong
admin@maradar.ai

13. How Can You Review, Update, or Delete the Data We Collect From You?

Based on the applicable laws of your country, you may have the right to request access to the personal information we collect from you, details about how we have processed it, correct inaccuracies, or delete your personal information. You may also have the right to withdraw your consent to our processing of your personal information. These rights may be limited in some circumstances by applicable law. To make a request, please contact us at admin@maradar.ai. Subject to our legal obligations, verified deletion requests will be processed in accordance with Section 7: a default 30-day data export window, followed by a further 60-day deletion period from active systems, with deletion from routine backups typically within 90 days. Aggregated and anonymised data, and information retained as required by applicable law, are excluded from these windows.

Cookie Policy

Last updated May 5, 2026

This Cookie Policy explains how Maradar Limited ("Company," "we," "us," and "our") uses cookies and similar technologies. It explains what these technologies are, why we use them, and your rights to control our use of them.

This Cookie Policy applies to two surfaces:

  1. Maradar's marketing website (maradar.ai) — where we may use cookies and similar technologies for marketing and advertising purposes, including audience tracking and remarketing through third-party platforms (such as Meta and Google).
  2. Maradar's authenticated application (app.maradar.ai) — where we use cookies strictly for essential, functional, and analytics purposes. We do not set advertising cookies or allow third-party advertising networks within the authenticated application. Data processed within the app environment is never shared with third-party advertising networks for remarketing or profiling purposes.

This separation is intentional: the marketing site is a public-facing site where commercial promotion is appropriate, while the authenticated application is where you do business with us, and we treat the authenticated environment as a higher-trust zone.

In some cases, we may use cookies to collect personal information, or that becomes personal information if we combine it with other information.

What are cookies?

Cookies are small data files that are placed on your computer or mobile device when you visit a website. Cookies are widely used by website owners in order to make their websites work, or to work more efficiently, as well as to provide reporting information.

Cookies set by the website owner (in this case, Maradar Limited) are called "first-party cookies." Cookies set by parties other than the website owner are called "third-party cookies." Third-party cookies enable third-party features or functionality to be provided on or through the website (e.g., advertising, interactive content, and analytics). The parties that set these third-party cookies can recognise your computer both when it visits the website in question and also when it visits certain other websites.

Why do we use cookies?

We use first- and third-party cookies for several reasons. Some cookies are required for technical reasons in order for our Services to operate, and we refer to these as "essential" or "strictly necessary" cookies. Other cookies enable us to track and target the interests of our users to enhance the experience on our Services. The specific cookies used differ between our marketing website and our authenticated application, as described below.

Cookies on the Maradar marketing website (maradar.ai)

When you visit our marketing website at maradar.ai, we may use the following categories of cookies:

  • Essential cookies: required for site functionality (loading, language preferences, basic operation).
  • Analytics cookies: help us understand how the marketing site is used so we can improve it.
  • Advertising and remarketing cookies: used by Maradar and our advertising partners (such as Meta and Google) to deliver relevant advertisements about Maradar's services to you when you visit other sites and to measure ad campaign performance.

Cookies on the Maradar authenticated application (app.maradar.ai)

When you use the authenticated application at app.maradar.ai, we use the following categories of cookies:

  • Essential cookies: required for authentication, session management, and security (set by Maradar and our authentication provider Supabase). These cannot be disabled.
  • Functional cookies: remember your preferences and settings within the application.
  • Analytics cookies: help us understand how the application is used so we can improve it.

We do not set advertising or third-party tracking cookies within the authenticated application.

How can I control cookies?

You have the right to decide whether to accept or reject non-essential cookies. You can manage your cookie preferences through your browser settings or, where available, our cookie consent banner. Essential cookies cannot be rejected as they are strictly necessary to provide the Services. If you choose to reject non-essential cookies, you may still use our Services, though access to some functionality may be restricted.

Cookie Consent for Hong Kong, EEA, UK, and other jurisdictions

Maradar provides clear notice of cookie use to all visitors. If you visit our Services from the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with strict cookie consent requirements, you will be presented with a cookie consent banner allowing you to accept or reject non-essential cookies (including advertising cookies). For visitors from Hong Kong and other jurisdictions, the banner provides an equivalent option to accept or decline non-essential cookies, consistent with the recommendations of the Hong Kong Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data and similar regulators.

How can I control cookies on my browser?

As the means by which you can refuse cookies through your web browser controls vary from browser to browser, you should visit your browser's help menu for more information. The following links provide information about how to manage cookies on the most popular browsers:

  • Chrome — Settings → Privacy and security → Cookies and other site data
  • Internet Explorer — Tools → Internet Options → Privacy
  • Firefox — Options → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data
  • Safari — Preferences → Privacy → Cookies and website data
  • Edge — Settings → Privacy, search, and services → Cookies and site permissions
  • Opera — Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies

To opt out of advertising cookies on a network-wide level, you may visit the following industry tools:

  • Digital Advertising Alliance: https://www.aboutads.info
  • European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance: https://www.youronlinechoices.eu
  • Australian Digital Advertising Alliance: https://youronlinechoices.com.au
  • Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada: https://youradchoices.ca

What about other tracking technologies, like web beacons?

Cookies are not the only way to recognise or track visitors to a website. We may use other, similar technologies from time to time, like web beacons (sometimes called "tracking pixels" or "clear gifs"). These are tiny graphics files that contain a unique identifier that enables us to recognise when someone has visited our Services or opened an email including them. This allows us, for example, to monitor the traffic patterns of users from one page within our Services to another, to deliver or communicate with cookies, to understand whether you have come to our Services from an online advertisement displayed on a third-party website, to improve site performance, and to measure the success of email marketing campaigns. In many instances, these technologies are reliant on cookies to function properly, and so declining cookies will impair their functioning.

Do you serve targeted advertising?

We may serve advertising about Maradar's services to you on third-party platforms (such as Meta and Google), including by using cookies and similar technologies on maradar.ai to identify users we have previously engaged with. This is sometimes referred to as remarketing or audience tracking, and it is limited to promoting Maradar's own services.

We do not sell personal information to third parties for their own commercial purposes. We do not allow third-party advertising networks to set cookies within our authenticated application at app.maradar.ai. Maradar's Services are designed for B2B marketing teams; we do not engage in cross-context behavioural advertising or share personal information for advertising purposes outside of promoting our own Services.

How often will you update this Cookie Policy?

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time in order to reflect, for example, changes to the cookies we use or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons. Please therefore revisit this Cookie Policy regularly to stay informed about our use of cookies and related technologies. The date at the top of this Cookie Policy indicates when it was last updated.

Where can I get further information?

If you have any questions about our use of cookies or other technologies, please contact us at:
